clue.text: Utterly economical?

parts.note: utterly is read as 'in the manner of uttering', so the phrase describes someone sparing with spoken words

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a person who is terse wastes no words, so is thrifty in speech.

clue.text: Not so much happening in the class?

parts.note: not so much means less
something happening is on, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: A dull schoolroom where less is going on than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a period of teaching at school is called a class.

clue.text: Fail to win in sporting contest through short-range shot

indicators.note: in places the losing word inside the word for the contest

parts.note: a cup is a knockout sporting competition, such as the FA Cup
to fail to win is to lose

explanation.surface: A footballer misses from a few yards and his side goes out of the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The shot looks like a striker's effort at goal; it is a photographer's or film-maker's. 'in' is the container signal, and 'through' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example from photography: a picture taken from very near the subject.

clue.text: Food Greek character set before sea-god capturing isle

indicators.note: set before tells us the Greek letter is placed ahead of the rest

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: capturing means the sea-god's name takes the isle's letter inside it

parts.note: Triton is a minor sea-god of Greek myth, son of Poseidon
I is a map abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: A meal is laid out for a Greek before a sea deity who is seizing an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of nourishment, what one eats to sustain the body.

clue.text: Entertaining ladies for kicks?

parts.note: the ladies are themselves the entertainers, and the kicks are the high kicks of a stage dance line

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: women in a stage dance line are known for their high leg movements.

clue.text: Almost tropical variety of fruit

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters take a new order
almost means the word is taken short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A fruit that is nearly, but not quite, from the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims tropical to TROPICA, and 'variety of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a soft orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Bristle left when the grass is cut

indicators.note: is cut tells us a letter is removed from the grass word

parts.note: a lawn is an area of mown grass

explanation.surface: The stubble remaining after someone has mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not what remains but the letter L, which 'is cut' from LAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term: the stiff hair on an ear of barley or other grasses.

clue.text: There's always upset about kind of turn seen in such entertainment

indicators.note: about means the upset word goes round the turn's letter
upset in a down clue means the word is overturned, read from the bottom up

parts.note: ever means always
a U-turn is one kind of turn, giving the letter U

explanation.surface: In variety shows somebody is always annoyed by one of the acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EVER into REVE, and 'about' puts U inside it. A turn is also a British word for a short stage act, which is what the surface means.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a stage show of sketches, songs and short acts.

clue.text: Firm has deficiency — one in large figures

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a deficiency in the accounts is a loss
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A company's accounts show a shortfall running to big numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures look like sums of money; they are giant statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the word for a gigantic statue, like the one at Rhodes.

clue.text: No record is kept by those people making a study in faith

indicators.note: is kept by means the pair of pieces is held inside the word for those people

parts.note: they is the pronoun for those people
O looks like zero, none
a log is a record of events

explanation.surface: A group researching religion keeps no written notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the academic discipline concerned with God and religious belief.

clue.text: A neat little instrument?

definitions.note: neat is an old word for an ox or cow, here one breed of cattle

parts.note: little in length is short
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A tidy, compact musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but the old noun for cattle, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a breed of cattle, neat being an archaic noun for a bovine animal.

clue.text: Dean, we hear, accepts University prize

indicators.note: accepts means the valley word takes the university's letter inside it
we hear says Dean is to be taken by ear, as its soundalike dene, a wooded valley, which then supplies its synonym

parts.note: said aloud this is dene, a small valley, for which the entered synonym is a four-letter word for a valley

explanation.surface: A college head is said to be taking an academic award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns Dean into its soundalike dene, a valley, and the entered piece is a synonym of that, VALE; 'accepts' puts U inside. The definition is a verb: to prize something is to esteem it highly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to esteem or treasure something highly.

clue.text: Daggers drawn in retrospect from puerile boyhood quarrel

indicators.note: drawn means pulled out, and in retrospect means looking backwards, so the letters are taken out in the opposite direction
from says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Knives come out years later over a childish playground row.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join of 'puerile boyhood', running right to left, as 'drawn in retrospect from' says. Daggers here are printers' marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing term: the plural of the dagger-shaped reference mark used for footnotes.

clue.text: Runs a live broadcast worldwide

indicators.note: broadcast originally means scattered, as seed is, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A television channel transmits a live programme across the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, rearranging 'Runs a live'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: applying everywhere, to all people and places.

clue.text: Depicted it all with rudest embellishment

indicators.note: embellishment is a decorative reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist drew the whole scene and added the crudest decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shown in pictures.

clue.text: Bound before punishment, holding leonine skin in this purification ritual

indicators.note: before says the leaping word comes ahead of the punishment

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap

indicators.note: holding means the punishment word has the skin letters inside it

parts.note: caning is beating with a cane, once a school punishment

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A captive is tied up, lion pelt in hand, ahead of a beating in some cleansing ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the annual thorough scrub of a house.

clue.text: Plucky maiden, entering unknown with leading Greek

indicators.note: entering means the first two pieces go inside the word for unknown

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, labels a work whose author is unknown
game means plucky, willing to have a go
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A brave girl walks into uncharted territory beside a Greek chieftain.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the king who commanded the Greek army at Troy.

clue.text: Put out about nothing, jolly tea-party attendant

indicators.note: about means the word for put out goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
O looks like zero, nothing
jolly is British naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A guest at tea who is cross over a trifle yet still cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is not cheerful but slang for a Royal Marine, RM. The tea party is the Mad Hatter's in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary reference: the sleepy guest at the Mad Hatter's table in Lewis Carroll's book.

clue.text: Many an order is a mistake for this mariner

indicators.note: a mistake is something gone wrong, so the letters before it are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A sailor finds that plenty of commands from above turn out to be blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a low rank of sailor in the Royal and merchant navies.

clue.text: Lowers animal conservation unit into lairs

indicators.note: into means the conservation vessel goes inside the lairs

parts.note: dens are the lairs of wild animals
Noah's ark saved the animals from the Flood, a playful conservation unit

explanation.surface: Wardens let a wildlife rescue crate down into the burrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' is not lets down: of the sky it means grows gloomy (also spelt lours).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the weather sense: a sky that lowers grows black and threatening.

clue.text: Chopped sausage to relieve hunger

indicators.note: chopped means cut into bits, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone slices up a banger to keep starvation at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ease or satisfy an appetite or pain.

clue.text: Cut new flower

definitions.note: read as flow-er, something that flows: a river

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament

explanation.surface: A freshly picked bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows: Britain's longest river, running from Wales to the Bristol Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a river, as a thing that flows.

clue.text: Water fowl circle a couple of poles by the river

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed (scan agrees): 'Water fowl circle a couple of poles by the river' (9) for MERGANSER. Apparent build is MERGE round A + NS, then R, but no clue word gives MERGE ('circle' is needed as the container indicator and 'Water fowl' as the definition); a search of the exact clue found no parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Water fowl circle a couple of poles by the river

clue.text: A reptile less likely to multiply?

definitions.meaning: a venomous snake, Britain's only one
someone who does sums of addition rather than multiplication

explanation.definitionFit: Both a viper and, whimsically, a person doing addition answer to this word.

clue.text: Points to a girl to follow

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are points of the compass
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at a young woman, telling another to go after her.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to come after as a result.

clue.text: Coup loses Commander before completion of overthrow

indicators.note: before places what is left of the first word ahead of the completion
loses means the commander's letters drop out of the first word

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer
the completion of something is its end

explanation.surface: A plot to seize power falls apart when its leader is removed before the government is toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to turn something over, to topple it.

clue.text: A sign the King is away — tea is made for the prince

indicators.note: is away means the King's letter is absent from the sign word

parts.note: a portent is a sign of things to come
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: is made means the tea letters are made up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A flag shows the monarch is out, so the afternoon brew is prepared for his son instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is away' removes R from PORTENT, and 'is made' rearranges tea into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a powerful ruler or monarch.

clue.text: Home for father with daughter

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A house for a dad and his girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: the place where one lives.

clue.text: Handed the blame — lack of care initially made it inevitable

indicators.note: lack of means the next-named letter is missing from the blame word

parts.note: someone censured has been formally blamed

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of care

explanation.surface: Once someone was held responsible, negligence at the outset meant the outcome was bound to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: guaranteed, made certain that it would happen.

clue.text: Tunnelled, taking a long time to grab a number out of cell

indicators.note: taking adds the long time after the digging word
to grab means the first two pieces together seize the number between them

parts.note: dug is what someone who tunnelled did
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A prisoner burrowed for years to get several inmates free.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an underground prison chamber.
